promptable_rule: When a prompt names face beauty/smoothness and a specific gaze direction, those clauses outrank raw muscle size in the owner's pick — select for the cleanest, prettiest face with the correct eyeline and keep energy VFX subtle enough not to obscure the muscle sculpt.

fav_vs_studio_pick.comparison: ae80ee28a5.jpg (Flow favorite) vs 65a129a178.jpg (Studio ownerManualPick): the favorite wins face beauty/smoothness, gaze compliance, and defect absence (65a1's viewer-left deltoid-bicep junction is slightly balloon-like and its two close onlookers have mildly rubbery faces); the Studio pick wins expression intensity (triumphant grin vs soft awe), growth payoff (bigger arms plus clapping/shocked witnesses = reaction-intercut), and shows more of the figure. I would keep 65a129a178.jpg for the page: the corpus rubric weights dead-face avoidance and escalation devices heavily, and its emotional register actually matches the 'The power, I can feel it' line, while its minor anatomy softness costs less than the favorite's understated face. ae80ee28a5.jpg is the better character-beauty reference, so it is worth banking as a ref-chain anchor even if 65a1 ships.

notes: The two owner signals disagree, and they map cleanly onto two value systems: the Flow favorite optimizes character rendering (beauty, cleanliness, eyeline), the Studio pick optimizes storytelling (expression, witnesses). The favorite's own weakness is emotional understatement relative to its excited dialogue. Batch-level: 11 of 12 rolls are near-identical framings, so this beat contributes to camera monotony regardless of pick; the favorite and the Studio pick are the only two that break the flat-frontal mold cleanly (7cde68ff71 breaks it too but with grotesque anatomy).
